title: Adaptive request coalescer and kernel hinting to reduce embedding endpoint tail latency
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Production embeddings endpoint is exhibiting long tail latency spikes on small concurrent requests and during low-traffic periods. Root cause signals point to high per-request overhead (scheduling + kernel start-up) and frequent KV cache cold misses for short sequences. This ticket implements an adaptive request coalescer (request folding + delay budget), kernel hinting to prefer warmed execution paths, and a lightweight KV prefetch probe to reduce p95/p99. Goal: reduce observed tail latency without increasing average token cost or degrading embedding quality.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for 64B request shape reduced from ~280ms to <=160ms under SLO workload (50 qps, 1-4 request batch sizes)
p95 improved to <=90ms and p50 unchanged or improved
no regression in embedding cosine similarity on regression suite (delta < 0.002 on representative dataset)
end-to-end throughput (qps) within 5% of baseline under sustained load
feature gated and configurable via runtime flags with 0-cost default when disabled
context_and_background: Observed patterns: tail spikes correlate with bursty single-request traffic and kernel cold start when model switching occurs.
Existing batching layer only groups requests per-epoch; small bursts often bypass batching resulting in many tiny kernel invocations.
KV cache hit-rate drops for varied request prefixes; cache warmup costs materialize as CPU/GPU stalls at kernel launch.

Previous attempts (ENG-25390, ENG-23812) focused on adaptive inflight coalescing and opportunistic merge — this work targets a complementary approach centered on short-delay coalescing and kernel-level hints.
work_items: Design adaptive coalescer: delay budget config, max-fold window, and priority based on route/tenant
Implement thread-local folding queue to avoid cross-core contention and keep batching cheap
Add kernel hint API: warm-path flag, preferred kernel selection hint for short-sequence fast path
KV prefetch probe: asynchronous warm probe for likely KV keys before kernel startup
Create experiment harness in loadgen to measure p50/p95/p99 across traffic shapes
Add feature flags and telemetry: fold rate, average delay added, kernel-hint hit-rate
Run canary on limited tenants; collect replayed traffic metrics and quality regressions
decisions: Use a short, tenant-configurable delay budget (default 8ms) rather than fixed-size microbatches to avoid unnecessary latency for single request flows.
Prefer local folding queues per worker to keep coalescing cheap and minimize rendezvous latency.
Expose kernel hint as a binary flag to runtime. Kernel will select warmed fast-path when hint=true and sequence length < threshold.
KV prefetch will be a best-effort asynchronous probe; failures must be non-fatal and non-blocking to the main request path.
Rollout as feature-gated canary: 1% tenants -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% based on telemetry and quality checks.
open_risks_and_blockers: Excessive coalescing delay could harm p50 for latency-sensitive customers if misconfigured.
Kernel hint misuse could select an incompatible kernel for rare model variants; require kernel compatibility checks.
KV prefetch increases GPU/CPU cycles for low-benefit cases; need cost model to avoid net cost regression.
Dependency on runtime API changes in serving; must coordinate with infra team (ENG-24681 style rollout).
updates: 2026-02-12: Initial profiling run showed p99=282ms, p95=112ms for 1-3 request burst shape. Tagged hotspots: kernel launch and initial KV fetch path.
2026-02-18: Prototype coalescer implemented (local folding queue). In synthetic tests, average added delay=6ms, p99 reduced ~40ms for small bursts.
2026-02-25: Kernel hint API merged behind flag (PR 2145). Warm-path selection reduces kernel startup by ~18ms in microbenchmarks.
2026-03-02: KV prefetch probe integrated; observed 7% increase in cache hit-rate on warm tenants but +2% CPU utilization on workers.
2026-03-08: Canary (1% tenants) deployed. Early telemetry: p99 down to ~170ms, p95 ~98ms. No quality regressions observed on nightly regression embeddings set.
2026-03-12: Review feedback from PM (Lina Torres) and Design (Marco R.) suggests adding tenant controls in Console and adding explanatory tooltips. UX ticket created.
next_steps: Address review feedback: Console control and tooltips (coordinate with product-management).
Run extended canary across more diverse models and sequence lengths for 48 hours to validate stability.
Add dynamic cost guard that disables KV prefetch under high worker CPU utilization.
Prepare rollout plan and postmortem checklist for problems during scale-up
Finalize documentation and add example SDK flags; ship with runtime-2.4 canary release
